raw_response.country: Global / multi-continental (World Water Forums held in Morocco, Netherlands, Japan, Mexico, Turkey, and France)

criterion_notes.c1: Does not examine actual household or community water or sanitation service access; instead analyzes how the human right to drinking water was framed in international declarations and final reports of the six World Water Forums (1997-2012).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 (plain = yes) because it discusses international human-rights norms (UDHR, ICESCR, General Comment No. 15), World Water Forum governance declarations, and constitutional recognition of the right to water (e.g., Uruguay, Bolivia, Ecuador). However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading (narrow = no) because it examines macro-level international conference rhetoric and normative human-rights declarations rather than any concrete rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism (such as eligibility rules, documentation/tenure requirements, tariff rules, enforcement, or utility regulation) directly governing service access. Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall full-text decision remains exclude because the paper lacks empirical service-access evidence and reports no service-access outcome.
criterion_notes.c3: No empirical evidence on water or sanitation service access (Exclusion Criteria 1 and 6). Although the authors apply qualitative textual analysis (citing Moraes 1999) and count occurrences of the keyword 'human right'/'human rights' across four World Water Forum final reports and two Forum webpages, this is a documentary/normative review of international conference declarations with no primary or empirical data on real-world water or sanitation access.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports only thematic framing of human-rights declarations, World Water Forum attendance totals, and relative shares of the keyword 'human rights' across Forum reports; no outcome measuring household or community water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion is reported.
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis is six World Water Forum reports/webpages (1997-2012); no household or community population, service-governing exposure, or service-access outcome is identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in Portuguese (with Portuguese and English abstracts), which is directly eligible without translation.

evidence_quotes.quote: Considerando o exposto, o objetivo deste estudo é compreender como a questão da água, enquanto direito humano, vem sendo tratada em nível continental nos Fóruns Mundiais da Água ocorridos entre os anos de 1997 e 2012, a partir da análise textual qualitativa.
Os documentos consultados nesta pesquisa foram extraídos dos Fóruns Mundiais da Água, sendo que a maioria das informações obtidas foi encontrada nos relatórios finais dos respectivos fóruns.
As informações coletadas referem-se à preocupação com a identificação do tratamento concebido à água na condição de direito humano. Para tanto, buscou-se pela palavra chave em inglês “human right”.

Quanto à ocorrência da palavra-chave “human rights”, constatou-se que 33% das ocorrências foram encontradas no 6º Fórum Mundial da Água, seguido do 5º Fórum e do 4º Fórum, os quais representam respectivamente cerca de 27% e 24% do total de ocorrências.

raw_response.outcome: Thematic framing of the human right to water in conference declarations, Forum attendance counts, and relative frequency of the keyword 'human right'/'human rights' across World Water Forum reports (no service-access outcome reported)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Documents from six World Water Forums (1997-2012): WWC webpages for the 1st and 2nd Forums and final reports for the 3rd, 4th (including continental reports), 5th, and 6th Forums; no household or community sample
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E05 (No empirical evidence; per Exclusion Criteria 1 and 6 on normative/doctrinal human-rights reviews without empirical access evidence). Zorzi, Turatti, and Mazzarino (2016) review webpages and final reports from the 1st through 6th World Water Forums (1997-2012) using a keyword search for 'human right' to describe how international and continental declarations framed the human right to drinking water. The study provides no empirical data on household or community water or sanitation service access (c1=no, c3=no), examines macro-level international conference rhetoric rather than a rule-type mechanism governing service access under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification (c2=no; though plain Criterion 2=yes, plain_criterion2_decision is still exclude), and reports only conference discourse, participant counts, and keyword shares rather than any service-access outcome (c4=no). Even if the documentary content analysis of Forum reports were treated as an empirical discourse study, it would still be excluded for lacking any household/community service-access outcome (E04) and lacking a rule-type exposure (E03).
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative textual/documentary analysis of World Water Forum final reports and webpages (1997-2012)
